unanticipated_findings: Undocumented permanent dedup collapse when X-Webhook-Delivery is omitted. service.py:115 falls back to `delivery_id = sha256(body).hexdigest()`, which contains no time component, and the deliveries table is never pruned. Two genuinely distinct events with byte-identical payloads from the same sender are therefore silently swallowed forever. Reproduced against a live server: two POSTs of body `{"event":"heartbeat"}` with no X-Webhook-Delivery header and timestamps 120 seconds apart returned `(202, accepted)` then `(200, duplicate)`. The README never mentions the fallback or its consequence; only tests/e2e/test_http.py:198-203 records the behaviour.

`webhook-receiver check` has a filesystem side effect its own help text disclaims. cli.py:53 describes the subcommand as 'valida a configuração e sai, sem subir nada', but comando_check calls `_abrir_banco` (cli.py:117), which runs `store.initialize()` and creates the database. Reproduced in an empty directory: `webhook-receiver check --db ./validate-only.db` printed `configuração ok` and left a 20480-byte `validate-only.db` behind. This is the command the README (line 119) recommends running during deploy before cutting over.

README prose is truncated in three places, mid-sentence. Line 7-9: 'O serviço roda. Os comandos abaixo funcionam numa máquina limpa, e a suíte / segundos.' (verb and number missing). Lines 183-184: 'A superfície completa, com todos os estados e o texto exato das mensagens, está' — the sentence ends, and the document it points to does not exist anywhere in the tree. Lines 253-254: 'Mudanças que alterem verificação de assinatura, deduplicação ou o contrato do' — the contribution rule is cut off before stating what such changes require. Reproduce by reading README.md.

The async dispatch path has no storage-error guard, unlike the request path. app.py:130 wraps `service.receive` in `except sqlite3.Error` and returns 503, but `service.dispatch` (service.py:151-169) calls `store.mark_failed` / `store.mark_handled` unguarded from inside a Starlette BackgroundTask. A transient sqlite error there escapes after the response has already been sent, leaves the row `pending` with the 300s lease still held by the dead task, and the delivery is invisible to recovery until that lease expires. No test covers this path.

`DeliveryStore.mark_handled(row_id, now)` accepts a `now` argument it never uses (store.py:229-238 — `now` appears in the signature but in neither the SQL nor the parameter tuple). Related: the same statement does `attempts = attempts + 1` on success, so a delivery handled correctly on the first try is recorded with `attempts = 1`; the live db dump shows `('acme','p1','handled',1,None,24)` for a delivery that was never retried.

The recovery loop processes its batch strictly serially: recovery.py:46-47 does `for entrega in entregas: await self.service.dispatch(entrega)` over a batch of up to 50 (DEFAULT_BATCH). Because dispatch awaits the user handler, one slow or hanging handler stalls every other recovered delivery in the batch and delays the next scan indefinitely — there is no per-dispatch timeout anywhere in the codebase.

No retention or pruning of any kind. Successfully handled rows keep the full request payload as a BLOB forever (store.py:30-47; nothing in the codebase deletes from `deliveries`). The database is therefore both an unbounded payload archive and an unbounded dedup index. The README roadmap (line 235) lists a retention policy only for dead-letters, not for handled deliveries.
